display.title: Episode 225: The Flickering Flame (Sefiras HaOmer)
display.summary_short: Why we count the Omer with excitement, how precious the gift of time is, and the story of a shoemaker whose flickering lamp taught a tzaddik that while the flame burns we can still repair.
display.summary_long: Recorded in the middle of Sefiras HaOmer. Uncle Yossi explains that we count the days to relive the excitement of the Jewish people as they waited for Matan Torah, and that every Jew had to be there, united like one person, the same unity that will bring Moshiach. A girl from Ann Arbor, Michigan, says the Shema in Studio 604. Next comes a talk on the gift of time: we cannot control time, only what we fill it with, and lost time never comes back, as in the story of a boy who keeps wishing for the dollar he lost. In the story, the tzaddik Reb Chaim is caught in a storm and finds Beryl the shoemaker still working late by the light of his lamp. Beryl says that as long as the lamp is burning, one can still repair. Reb Chaim, following the Baal Shem Tov's teaching to learn from everything, explains that as long as the soul is in the body we can still fix our mistakes and do mitzvos. The show ends with a contest update.
display.lesson: Time is a precious gift from Hashem: fill it with Torah and mitzvos, because as long as the flame burns we can still repair and do good.
